text:
jess: Starting tiny canary for rwd-v3.1-int4-longctx on 3% traffic. Goal: validate long-doc citation fidelity after recent int4 quant pass. Will watch longdoc_mrr and token-divergence.

omar: paste quick snapshot when available pls.

jess: quick numbers: baseline p95 430ms | longdoc_mrr 0.846 | cit_hallu 0.85%
canary(3%) p95 360ms | longdoc_mrr 0.838 | cit_hallu 1.7%

neha: latency looks great but citation hallu doubled. Suggest immediate mitigations: (1) drop canary to 0.5%, (2) enable kv-prefix warmup for longctx routes, (3) run deterministic shadow-compare on citation slice.

jess: lowering now. @runtime-bot set-canary rwd-v3.1-int4-longctx 0.5% --note "limit exposure due to cit_hallu"

runtime-bot: Canary updated: rwd-v3.1-int4-longctx scaled to 0.5% (requested by jess).

omar: run eval: `/eval run --suite citation_longdoc --model rwd-v3.1-int4-longctx --control rwd-v3.0-fp16 --deterministic --topk 40 --sample 0.5%` ETA ~9m

neha: proposing auto-fallback rules to add to console (temporary):
- longdoc_mrr_drop >= 0.8% over 10m -> revert to rwd-v3.0-fp16
- token_divergence_pct >= 1.25% over 5m -> revert to rwd-v3.0-fp16

jess: enabling kv_warmup_ratio 0.5 for longctx routes (runtime tweak).

omar: eval done: token divergence concentrated at citation boundaries = 1.5% vs control, 3 examples with invented refs. This breaches the token_divergence guard.

neha: manual rollback recommended. I'll also add a P1 alert rule and update the runbook with those guards.

jess: rolling back now. @runtime-bot revert rwd-v3.1-int4-longctx --to rwd-v3.0-fp16 --note "rollback after citation divergence"

runtime-bot: Revert initiated. Traffic restored to rwd-v3.0-fp16 for impacted routes.

omar: follow-ups: per-layer quant sensitivity sweep (owner: neha), outlier-aware quant pass, and tighter token-divergence gating for future canaries. Keep thread for updates.

jess: thanks — short lived canary, rollback done, filing reproducer and anonymized examples to eng-ml-priv.
